bull_bear.body:
- Long-standing trusted global partnerships with leading chemical manufacturers, particularly in Japan, Germany and Thailand, underpinning both distribution sourcing and manufacturing technology collaboration
- South Asia's first bio-catalytic acrylamide manufacturing facility under licensed technology in technical collaboration with Mitsui Chemicals, Inc., Japan
- Only manufacturer of Acrylamide Solid outside China, providing a differentiated supply-chain-diversification alternative
- Only merchant manufacturer of N-Methylol Acrylamide (NMA) in India, a niche specialty chemical segment with limited domestic competition
- International product registrations (REACH, KKDIK) supporting access to European and Turkish markets
- Established stock-and-sale distribution model supporting reliable product availability and working-capital efficiency
- Integrated distribution-plus-manufacturing platform where customer/supplier insights from distribution inform manufacturing priorities and vice versa
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Key management succession risk — The absence of an effective succession framework for key managerial personnel could impact leadership continuity, strategic execution, and stakeholder confidence.
- Supply chain / supplier concentration risk — Dependence on key suppliers or principals may lead to disruptions in procurement and business operations in the event of unexpected supply discontinuation; the distribution business relies on long-standing principal relationships, particularly in Japan, Germany and Thailand.
- Compliance and regulatory (environmental/EHS) risk — Failure to comply with applicable statutory, environmental, health, safety and regulatory requirements could result in penalties, operational restrictions and reputational impact; the Jhagadia manufacturing facility received GPCB closure directions during the year (later revoked), evidencing this exposure is live rather than theoretical.
- Geopolitical risk — Trade restrictions, tariffs, sanctions, geopolitical tensions and ongoing conflicts (including instability in the Middle East) may disrupt global supply chains, increase logistics costs, constrain raw-material availability and heighten uncertainty in international markets.
- Foreign exchange risk — Volatility in foreign currency markets may adversely affect earnings and cash flows arising from import and export transactions, given the Company's reliance on cross-border sourcing and merchant exports.
- Market / import-competition risk — Increasing competition from imported and domestic alternatives (including pricing pressure from Chinese imports noted for acrylamide solid) may pressure market share, pricing and profitability.
- Product liability / operational risk — Product quality issues or defects in regulated international markets may expose the Company to financial liabilities, legal proceedings and reputational risk, relevant given its REACH/KKDIK-registered export markets.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company operates two segments: Chemical Distribution, which imports, exports and markets a broad portfolio of specialty and performance chemicals sourced from leading global manufacturers (largest revenue contributor, ~64% of turnover); and Chemical Manufacturing, anchored in acrylamide chemistry, producing Acrylamide Liquid, Acrylamide Solid and N-Methylol Acrylamide (NMA) at its Jhagadia, Gujarat facility. It serves a diversified customer base across pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, polymers, textiles, rubber, ceramics and water treatment sectors, with sales predominantly domestic (~85%) and the balance exports.

outlook.body:
- Strengthen position across the chemical value chain, expand international presence, and build new platforms for growth
- Sharpened strategic focus on the upstream acrylamide value chain and other specialty chemical segments offering sustainable growth potential
- In manufacturing: increase volumes across key products, improve efficiencies, and advance the development pipeline
- In distribution: expand the product portfolio, strengthen principal partnerships, broaden the customer base, and grow international presence
- Deliberate decision to discontinue the polyacrylamide liquid business and exit the ceramic binder segment in Morbi, reallocating resources to areas of stronger long-term potential aligned with core acrylamide-chemistry expertise
- Building a broader specialty chemicals platform through innovation, technology development, and selective investments in attractive niche segments
- Continue to evaluate opportunities in specialty chemicals and adjacent chemistries that leverage existing manufacturing capabilities and market relationships
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company's Chemical Manufacturing platform at Jhagadia, Gujarat is anchored in acrylamide chemistry and its downstream derivatives, supported by scalable infrastructure and a growing land footprint. During 2025-26, the Company inaugurated a new, state-of-the-art R&D Centre in Navi Mumbai, strengthening product development, commercialisation and application-development capabilities. The Polyacrylamide (PAM) Solid project, targeting an installed capacity of 10,000 MTPA, advanced to the pilot stage during the year, alongside development of additional downstream acrylamide-chemistry products. The Company also initiated a feasibility study with Koei Chemical Company Limited, Japan, to evaluate the manufacture of specialty amine products in India, and continues to evaluate opportunities in adjacent chemistries and specialty chemical segments to diversify its portfolio and expand its addressable market. Conversely, the Company made a deliberate decision during the year to discontinue its polyacrylamide liquid business and exit the ceramic binder segment in Morbi, reallocating resources toward areas of stronger long-term potential aligned with its core acrylamide-chemistry expertise.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Rising specialty chemical demand, supply chain diversification, import substitution opportunities, and India's growing importance in global manufacturing support the Company's long-term growth positioning
- Distribution business outlook is positive, supported by stable industrial demand, improving export opportunities, and the potential to deepen relationships with existing customers while expanding into new applications and markets
- Manufacturing business expected to benefit from continued growth in domestic demand, increasing export opportunities, and ongoing global supply chain diversification initiatives, with acrylamide liquid, acrylamide solid and NMA remaining the principal growth drivers
- A relatively stable raw material environment, combined with focus on operational excellence, product quality, innovation and customer service, is expected to support sustainable growth and healthy profitability over the medium term
- China Plus One strategy has strengthened India's position as a preferred manufacturing destination, creating opportunities for domestic chemical producers with strong process expertise and quality standards
- Export demand improved towards the end of 2025-26, resulting in a recovery in merchant export volumes and a stronger order pipeline entering the new financial year
- Distribution business entered 2026-27 with a healthier customer pipeline after export demand remained subdued during parts of 2025-26
